messages:
customer_jordan: Hi, our web app is seeing SSE disconnects mid-stream on Chrome (Android) whenever users switch from cellular -> office Wi‑Fi. The server sometimes sends the final chunk but the client never gets it. Any ideas?

sophia_support: Sorry you're hitting this — can you share a minimal repro and any request/response logs? Is this with EventSource or a custom fetch/sse client?

customer_jordan: Using EventSource. Repro is easy: load chat, start generation, then move from 4G -> corporate Wi‑Fi. Happens ~60% of the time. We also noticed duplicate billing for a single message occasionally.

sophia_support: Yikes. Can you grab the browser console + server side connection logs for one instance? Also which token scheme are you using (long-lived API key vs short-lived JWT refresh)?

customer_jordan: Short-lived JWT rotated every 5m. Console shows: 

```
EventSource failed to connect
EventSource closed, status 0
Uncaught SyntaxError: Unexpected end of JSON input
```

Server side (excerpt):

```
[2026-03-12T15:02:17Z] conn=abcd1234 client_ip=10.2.3.4 status=200 sent=3580
[2026-03-12T15:02:18Z] conn=abcd1234 client_ip=10.2.3.4 error=TLS_read: Connection reset by peer
[2026-03-12T15:02:18Z] conn=abcd1234 closed_by=client
```

There was also a token refresh around 15:02:18.

devon_runtime: Thanks — two likely suspects: (1) client TCP/TLS reset during network handoff (NAT re-bind) and (2) token rotation race where the client refresh closes and re-opens EventSource while the old connection is torn down mid-chunk. Either can produce partial output + ECONNRESET.

sophia_support: Repro steps request to dev: can you try with longer JWT TTL and with EventSource reconnect backoff disabled? Also try sending keepalive heartbeats every 20s.

devon_runtime: Will try. Quick test plan: 1) reproduce with current app, 2) reproduce with JWT TTL bumped to 30m, 3) force network switch on emulator, 4) enable lightweight keepalive frames (server-side), 5) capture packet trace.

alex_billing: Regarding duplicate billing — when the client reconnects mid-stream and the server had already counted tokens for the partially-sent response, our billing pipeline sees the second connection as a fresh request and charges again. We need to know if the client delivered any acknowledgement for the partial payload.

customer_jordan: Client didn't ack. The UI shows partial message like "...and then the model said" and then nothing. Users refresh and sometimes they get a fresh full completion (charged again).

sophia_support: Short term mitigation: increase client-side debounce on reconnects and suppress new requests within 10s of a reconnect for the same prompt. Also try server-side idempotency keys for streaming sessions so duplicate billing can be detected.

devon_runtime: Update from my repro: I forced an emulator handoff and saw the same reset. When I disable JWT rotation and keep the same token, EventSource survives the handoff more reliably. With rotation turned on, I reproduce a client-initiated close on token refresh. Stack trace in browser shows the app calling `es.close()` before re-instantiating on token refresh.

sophia_support: That explains the mid-chunk truncation — client is actively closing before it has consumed remaining bytes. Can you share the refresh code?

customer_jordan: It's basically: 

```js
async function refreshToken() {
  const t = await fetch('/auth/refresh');
  eventSource.close();
  eventSource = new EventSource(`/sse?token=${t}`);
}
```

We were told to close and re-open immediately.

devon_runtime: That's the race — closing the ES instance causes the TCP close to be sent to the server which may interrupt a response mid-chunk. Two possible fixes: (A) switch to using short reconnect window where you don't call `.close()` until the server signals chunk boundary OR (B) use a background token refresh strategy that silently updates the token used for future connections and preserves the current stream until it ends.

eng-oncall: Pushing this to eng-runtime for a server-side improvement: we can add a small grace period on connection close detection where, if a client closes and then immediately reconnects with the same session-id within N seconds, we mark the prior in-flight request as resumed instead of double-billing. Will open an internal task.

infra-bot: Created task RT-9872 in eng-runtime: "SSE connection close grace + idempotency for streaming sessions" assigned to devon_runtime.

alex_billing: For billing immediate fix, we'll add a 10s dedupe window for streaming session charges keyed by customer_id + session_signature. That should reduce duplicates while we build the resume flow.

customer_jordan: Thanks — any workaround we can apply today on our side?

sophia_support: 1) Delay calling `es.close()` until you get an explicit complete/error event or a short timeout (e.g., 3s) after initiating refresh. 2) Increase token TTL as a stopgap to avoid mid-request rotation. 3) Implement UI dedupe where you suppress duplicate send attempts for an active prompt.

customer_jordan: We'll try the `.close()` delay and token TTL. I'll report back with logs. Really appreciate the quick triage. :pray: 

devon_runtime: One more note — if your users are switching to corporate Wi‑Fi that uses an intercepting proxy, that can also cause TLS resets. Packet capture will confirm.

sophia_support: Closing loop: created support ticket SUP-4902 and linked RT-9872 + billing task BILL-233. We'll follow up once eng-runtime has a patch.

customer_jordan: Got it, thank you all."
